chapter.title: Paper and Paperboard; Articles of Paper Pulp, of Paper or of Paperboard

page.h1: HTS Chapter 48: Paper and Paperboard; Articles of Paper Pulp, of Paper or of Paperboard — U.S. Exports & Foreign Tariffs

seo.title: U.S. Paper & Kraft Linerboard Exports by Country (HTS Ch. 48) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: U.S. paper and paperboard exports were $14.31B in 2025, down 7.4%; Canada and Mexico buy 67%. Kraftliner, boxes and coated board, and what buyers charge.

intro:
The U.S. exported **$14.31B** of paper, paperboard and paper products in 2025, down 7.4% on 2024 and 16% below the 2022 peak ($16.98B). Unbleached kraft linerboard (kraftliner, 4804.11) is the largest single line at **$2.21B**, and kraft paper and board as a group (4804) take **22%** ($3.14B). Boxes, cartons and bags (4819, $2.22B, led by corrugated boxes at $1.31B), plastic-coated and self-adhesive paper (4811, $1.96B), clay-coated paper and board (4810, $1.59B) and fluting and testliner (4805, $1.32B) follow. **Canada ($5.56B) and Mexico ($4.00B) buy 67%** between them; China bought $352M, down 37.6%.

Most of this trade pays no tariff: Mexico, Costa Rica and Guatemala charge nothing on paper that qualifies for their trade agreements, and the EU, the UK, Japan and Canada charge 0% on paper even without one. Two buyers charge more. **Canada** has charged a counter-surtax since September 8, 2026 on 17 paper tariff items, even when they qualify for CUSMA: **50%** on corrugated boxes, paper bags, tissue parent rolls, several coated papers and boards, envelopes, notebooks and paper cups and trays, and **25%** on toilet paper, facial tissue and towels. **China** adds a 10% extra duty to its 2–7.5% rates, its 2018–2019 counter-tariffs apply on top unless the buyer holds an exclusion, and U.S. unbleached sack kraft pays a 14.9% anti-dumping duty. Paper needs no product approval in these markets; the bigger compliance change is the EU deforestation rules, which reach paper from December 30, 2026.

keyTakeaways: U.S. Chapter 48 exports fell 7.4% to $14.31B in 2025 and another 6.8% in January–August 2026 ($9.20B); kraftliner (4804.11, $2.21B) and corrugated boxes (4819.10, $1.31B) are the two largest lines.

Canada, the largest buyer ($5.56B), charges a 50% surtax on U.S. corrugated boxes, bags, tissue parent rolls and several coated boards and 25% on toilet paper, tissues and towels since September 8, 2026; kraftliner, fluting, folding cartons and uncoated printing paper are not on its list, and buyers that use the goods in manufacturing or to package food or drink can claim the surtax back.

Mexico ($4.00B) charges nothing on paper that meets the USMCA rule of origin, which paper made in a U.S. mill from pulp meets wherever the pulp came from; since January 1, 2026 non-qualifying boxes, coated board and uncoated printing paper pay 25–35%.

China charges 15–17.5% on most U.S. paper before its older counter-tariffs, and exports there fell 37.6% to $352M; watch December 31, 2026 (exclusions end), January 10, 2027 (24-point suspension ends) and April 9, 2027 (sack kraft anti-dumping duty expires unless reviewed).
